Lisa, Hiro — attaching a compact artifacts bundle: siem_masking_patterns.yaml and a preliminary egress_validation_checklist.pdf. See highlights below.

Masking guidance (summary):
- Prefer upstream masking (agent/sidecar before egress) for PII (SSNs, emails, account IDs). Agent-level masking reduces blast radius and keeps telemetry minimal in transit.
- We support three masking modes: redact (replace with <REDACTED>), tokenize (deterministic hashing with tenant KMS), and pseudonymize (per-tenant salt). Tokenize requires a KMS-backed key; we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM or use RW-managed key under an MPO contract.
- Example regex patterns (from siem_masking_patterns.yaml):
  - email: '\b[\w.%-]+@[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,6}\b'
  - ssn: '\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b'
  - acct_id: 'acct_[A-Za-z0-9]{8,12}'

Forwarder vs edge: if you already have an internal forwarder that can be validated by security (Splunk UF, rsyslog, or a Kafka sink), we recommend masking at that forwarder and performing an additional light validation (schema stripping) at Redwood's ingress. If customers cannot host forwarder logic, we deploy a small sidecar proxy inside the VPC to do masking before outbound.

Network & transport:
- Mutual TLS (mTLS) between the forwarder and the Redwood collector is supported. We recommend certificate pinning for long-lived collectors.
- Ports: outbound 443 (HEC) or 514/UDP for syslog is supported but must be allowed in your egress policy.

Acceptance criteria (from checklist):
- No PII in sample telemetry (we'll provide a red-team sample).
- End-to-end TLS with mTLS validation and cert expiry checks.
- Signed egress validation checklist and list of allowed IP ranges.

Attachments: siem_masking_patterns.yaml (sample patterns), egress_validation_checklist.pdf

- Kim

Lisa, Kim — quick additions to make the checklist operational. See runbook items below (I pasted into the meeting notes doc we referenced: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/siem-masking-v1).

Runbook (pilot scope):
- Inventory: produce a short list of hostnames/IP ranges and forwarder types in your VPC (due EOD Thu).
- Config: deliver one sample payload with sensitive fields marked; Redwood will run a local test harness to show masking result.
- KMS: if you use customer-managed KMS, provide key ARN and test credentials (secure upload flow). If not, we'll provide a managed-key contract amendment.
- Egress validation tests:
  - Blocklist & allowlist tests (we'll send probe requests from the collector to ensure only allowed IPs are contacted).
  - mTLS handshake test using your cert chain.
- Performance baseline: run a 30-minute load with representative token rates and capture memory/CPU from the sidecar. Typical numbers (approx): 50MB RAM, 150m CPU per 100 req/s for the Go-based masking agent. We'll produce a small perf harness.

Acceptance criteria (short):
1) Red-team sample shows no PII leaving the tenant.
2) All collector egress matches the signed IP allowlist.
3) mTLS validated and cert chain accepted in our mutual test.
4) Performance within your thresholds (we'll agree on exact SLOs in the pilot doc).

I'll update the egress_validation_checklist.pdf to include these test steps and add a signature block for both teams.

—Marissa
